# **TABLE 8.19:** Energy savings for different application data

| Signal Type | *N* Symbol Frequency | TX Energy Savings Generated: Noiseless Channel | TX Energy Savings Generated: CNS |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ECG signals | 47.51% | 73.75% | 50% |
| JPEG blood/tissue sample images | 28.84% | 64.02% | 33% |

![](bbox=[0.24, 0.271, 0.761, 0.531])

**FIGURE 8.22:** Comparison of energy savings generated by CNS and RBN-SizeComm at transmitter for various application data types to binary FSK

We can thus conclude that CNS provides energy savings at both the transmitter and the receiver. The sum of transmitter and receiver energy savings offered by CNS over conventional EbT schemes employing BFSK, is more than that with RB-NSiZEComm and TSS. Thus, CNS will be very useful in real-life low-power applications, e.g., in wireless sensor networks and ad hoc networks where multi-hop wireless communication will be involved.
